> Abstract:While the critical points of the loss landscape in linear neural networks have been extensively studied since the seminal work of Baldi \& Hornik in the late 1980s, a description of this landscape at an intermediate or global scale is still lacking. Such a characterization is crucial, particularly as a substantial body of literature indicates that gradient descent circumvents critical points. The present article introduces an intermediate structure, termed the critical thalweg, which encompasses all critical points and exhibits key geometric properties.
Beyond providing a geometric proof of Baldi \& Hornik's results using simpler assumptions than the existing literature, this framework offers a global view of the loss landscape that can be easily visualized in a two-dimensional plane. Empirical observations suggest that gradient descent is attracted toward the critical thalweg, along which the loss continues to decrease to its global minimum.

# On the loss landscape of the linear neural network: beyond critical points
Computer Science > Machine Learning
[Submitted on 19 Nov 2026]
**Authors:** Antoine Lejay (PASTA, IECL), Lionel Lenotre (Universit{é} de Haute-Alsace (UHA)), Sa{ï}d Toubra (IECL)
## Abstract
While the critical points of the loss landscape in linear neural networks have been extensively studied since the seminal work of Baldi \& Hornik in the late 1980s, a description of this landscape at an intermediate or global scale is still lacking. Such a characterization is crucial, particularly as a substantial body of literature indicates that gradient descent circumvents critical points. The present article introduces an intermediate structure, termed the critical thalweg, which encompasses all critical points and exhibits key geometric properties. Beyond providing a geometric proof of Baldi \& Hornik's results using simpler assumptions than the existing literature, this framework offers a global view of the loss landscape that can be easily visualized in a two-dimensional plane. Empirical observations suggest that gradient descent is attracted toward the critical thalweg, along which the loss continues to decrease to its global minimum.
- **Subjects** Machine Learning (cs.LG); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Neural and Evolutionary Computing (cs.NE); Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Abstract

Multi-agent systems (MAS) usually coordinate heterogeneous models and tools to solve complex tasks, creating a growing need for reliable evaluation. However, a multi-agent workflow that is fastest in one serving environment can lose its advantage in another, even when its models, prompts, and task remain fixed. In a controlled motivation diagnostic, the Star workflow falls from first to fourth in mean-latency rank under KV-cache pressure, while Chain rises from fourth to first. The substrate sweeps further show that increasing load creates long runtime tails and timeout pressure.

octen.snippet:
# Complex band-limited maximum likelihood: estimating the wave behind detected quanta

arXiv:2611.28572
Authors: Rahul Agarwal, Ankit Agarwal
Submitted: 2026-11-21
Subjects: stat.ML cs.LG
Comments: 13 pages, 6 figures; supplementary material as ancillary file. Submitted to Physical Review A

Abstract

Detected photons and electrons land at positions drawn from $|\psi|^2$, yet it is $\psi$, phase included, that a wave equation propagates, and the state that produced the particles is often known only in part. A density estimator can recover $|\psi|^2$ directly from the positions, without any wave equation, but it discards the phase, and with it the state. We introduce complex band-limited maximum likelihood (complex BLML), which estimates $\psi$ itself by maximising the likelihood of the detected positions over exactly the intensities the physics allows: squared moduli of complex functions whose spectrum lies in a given set, such as a band, the shape of the aperture, or several modes for a partially coherent source. A single eigenvalue can certify a global maximum. On simulated two-slit far fields we measure what each prior is worth: a band reaches a given accuracy with seven times fewer photons than a kernel density estimate and already gives the fringe contrast and the relative phase, and the shape of the aperture adds the slit geometry. Some quantities need a prior at any number of photons: for slits of one profile the intensity fixes only the contrast $2\rho V/(1+\rho^2)$, and on a line two different apertures can produce the same particles.

Abstract: While the critical points of the loss landscape in linear neural networks have been extensively studied since the seminal work of Baldi \& Hornik in the late 1980s, a description of this landscape at an intermediate or global scale is still lacking. The present article introduces an intermediate structure, termed the critical thalweg, which encompasses all critical points and exhibits key geometric properties. # On the loss landscape of the linear neural network: beyond critical points
Computer Science > Machine Learning
[Submitted on 19 Nov 2026]
**Authors:** Antoine Lejay (PASTA, IECL), Lionel Lenotre (Universit{é} de Haute-Alsace (UHA)), Sa{ï}d Toubra (IECL)
## Abstract
While the critical points of the loss landscape in linear neural networks have been extensively studied since the seminal work of Baldi \& Hornik in the late 1980s, a description of this landscape at an intermediate or global scale is still lacking. Such a characterization is crucial, particularly as a substantial body of literature indicates that gradient descent circumvents critical points. The present article introduces an intermediate structure, termed the critical thalweg, which encompasses all critical points and exhibits key geometric properties. Beyond providing a geometric proof of Baldi \& Hornik's results using simpler assumptions than the existing literature, this framework offers a global view of the loss landscape that can be easily visualized in a two-dimensional plane. Empirical observations suggest that gradient descent is attracted toward the critical thalweg, along which the loss continues to decrease to its global minimum.
